title: Speed Run: Comprehensive Cognitive & Social Psych

questions.question: In a normal distribution of standardized WAIS intelligence scores (M=100, SD=15), approximately 68% of the population scores between 85 and 115.
questions.explanation: True. In a normal bell curve, 68.2% of all values fall within ±1 standard deviation of the mean.

questions.question: Which cognitive shortcut leads people to overestimate the danger of a plane crash because dramatic crashes are easily retrieved from memory?
questions.explanation: The availability heuristic estimates frequency based on ease of mental recall.

questions.question: In Stanley Milgram's classic obedience studies, what proportion of participants delivered the maximum 450-volt shock?
questions.explanation: Two-thirds (65%) of ordinary participants administered the maximum electrical shock under authority commands.

questions.question: According to Jean Piaget, during which stage does a child first master the principle of Conservation?
questions.explanation: Concrete operational children grasp conservation of volume, mass, and number.

questions.question: Mary Ainsworth classified infants who become distressed upon mother's departure but are quickly comforted upon her return as having:
questions.explanation: Secure attachment is shown by using the caregiver as a haven of safety and being easily soothed.

questions.question: The reduction in personal effort that occurs when individuals pool their work together in a collective group is known as:
questions.explanation: Social loafing is the drop in personal exertion when responsibility is shared.

questions.question: Which Big Five personality dimension describes an individual who is highly organized, dependable, disciplined, and goal-oriented?
questions.explanation: Conscientiousness reflects self-discipline, orderliness, and reliability.

questions.question: Retroactive interference occurs when previously learned old memories prevent you from remembering newly acquired information.
questions.explanation: False. Old memories disrupting new recall is Proactive interference. Retroactive interference is when new learning disrupts old recall.
